papers.title: ENHANCED TRIBOLOGICAL, MECHANICAL AND CORROSION PERFORMANCE OF MO AND NICR COATINGS ON LMD TI6AL4V ALLOY DEPOSITED VIA ATMOSPHERIC PLASMA SPRAYING IN A SELF -GOVERNMENT- DEVELOPED TECHNOLOGIES
papers.abstract: In this study, Ti-6Al-4V (Grade 5) alloy components were fabricated via Laser Metal Deposition (LMD) and subsequently coated with Nickel-Chromium (NiCr 80/20) and Molybdenum (Mo) powders using Atmospheric Plasma Spray (APS) to enhance their surface durability. The objective was to evaluate the synergistic effects of LMD and plasma spray coatings on the mechanical, tribological and corrosion properties of the Ti alloy. Microstructural and chemical analyses using SEM and EDS confirmed dense, uniform coatings with strong metallurgical bonding and minimal porosity. Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) revealed refined surface topographies, with Mo-coated samples exhibiting smoother profiles (Ra = 0.42 µm) compared to NiCr (Ra = 0.51 µm), facilitating better tribological contact. Vickers microhardness tests indicated significant surface strengthening, with hardness values increasing from 368 HV (uncoated) to 584.67 HV (Mo) and 537.66 HV (NiCr). Dry sliding wear tests demonstrated that Mo coatings provided superior wear resistance, with the lowest coefficient of friction (0.32) and specific wear rate (0.5 × 10⁻⁴ mm³/Nm), attributed to the formation of MoO₃ tribolayers. Electrochemical corrosion testing in 3.5% NaCl solution revealed that NiCr coatings outperformed Mo in corrosion protection, exhibiting a more noble corrosion potential (–450 mV) and significantly reduced current density (1.2 × 10⁻⁷ mA/cm²) due to the formation of a stable Cr₂O₃ passive film. These findings establish that integrating LMD with tailored plasma spray coatings enables surface-functionalized Ti alloys suitable for high-performance applications requiring enhanced wear and corrosion resistance.
papers.venue: Lex localis - Journal of Local Self-Government

llm.relevance_to_user: 本文涉及LMD Ti-6Al-4V的涂层性能，但未研究基体本身的力学和疲劳，与方向的核心关注点偏差较大。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on surface coatings (Mo/NiCr) deposited on LMD Ti-6Al-4V rather than the base material's mechanical or fatigue properties; no tensile, fatigue, or S-N data are reported.

summary_zh.motivation: 在激光金属沉积Ti-6Al-4V上喷涂Mo和NiCr涂层以提升表面性能。
summary_zh.method: 采用大气等离子喷涂制备涂层，通过SEM、AFM、硬度、磨损和腐蚀测试表征。
summary_zh.result: Mo涂层耐磨性最优，NiCr涂层耐腐蚀性更佳。
summary_zh.validation: 通过磨损、腐蚀实验和微观分析验证性能。

summary_en.motivation: To enhance the surface durability of LMD Ti-6Al-4V alloy by depositing Mo and NiCr coatings via atmospheric plasma spraying.
summary_en.method: Atmospheric plasma spraying was used to apply Mo and NiCr coatings on LMD Ti-6Al-4V substrates, followed by microstructural, mechanical, tribological, and corrosion characterization.
summary_en.result: Mo coatings exhibited superior wear resistance due to MoO3 tribolayers, while NiCr coatings provided better corrosion protection via Cr2O3 passive film.
summary_en.validation: Validation included SEM/EDS, AFM, microhardness, dry sliding wear tests, and electrochemical corrosion tests in 3.5% NaCl solution.

papers.title: Predicting Stress-strain Behaviors of Additively Manufactured Materials via Loss-based and Activation-based Physics-informed Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Predicting the stress-strain behaviors of additively manufactured materials is crucial for part qualification in additive manufacturing (AM). Conventional physics-based constitutive models often oversimplify material properties, while data-driven machine learning (ML) models often lack physical consistency and interpretability. To address these issues, we propose a physics-informed machine learning (PIML) framework to improve the predictive performance and physical consistency for predicting the stress-strain curves of additively manufactured polymers and metals. A polynomial regression model is used to predict the yield point from AM process parameters, then stress-strain curves are segmented into elastic and plastic regions. Two long short-term memory (LSTM) models are trained to predict two regions separately. For the elastic region, Hooke's law is embedded into the LSTM model for both polymer and metal. For the plastic region, Voce hardening law and Hollomon's law are embedded into the LSTM model for polymer and metal, respectively. The loss-based and activation-based PIML architectures are developed by embedding the physical laws into the loss and activation functions, respectively. The performance of the two PIML architectures are compared with two LSTM-based ML models, three additional ML models, and a physics-based constitutive model. These models are built on experimental data collected from two additively manufactured polymers (i.e., Nylon and carbon fiber-acrylonitrile butadiene styrene) and two additively manufactured metals (i.e., AlSi10Mg and Ti6Al4V). Experimental results demonstrate that two PIML architectures consistently outperform the other models. The segmental predictive model with activation-based PIML architecture achieves the lowest MAPE of 10.46+/-0.81% and the highest R^2 of 0.82+/-0.05 arocss four datasets.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文提出了一种物理信息机器学习框架，可预测Ti6Al4V等增材制造材料的应力-应变行为，但其主要贡献在于方法而非Ti6Al4V的力学性能本身。
llm.why_not_core: The paper does not provide new experimental data or insights specific to Ti-6Al-4V mechanical or fatigue characterization; it presents a general predictive framework tested on multiple materials including Ti6Al4V.

summary_zh.motivation: 传统本构模型和纯数据驱动模型在预测增材制造材料应力-应变行为时各有局限。
summary_zh.method: 提出基于物理信息机器学习（PIML）的分段预测框架，弹性段嵌入胡克定律，塑性段嵌入Voce或Hollomon硬化律，采用LSTM模型分别预测。
summary_zh.result: 激活式PIML架构在包括Ti6Al4V在内的四种材料数据集上取得最低MAPE 10.46%和最高R² 0.82。
summary_zh.validation: 使用尼龙、碳纤维ABS、AlSi10Mg和Ti6Al4V四种增材制造材料的实验数据进行验证。

summary_en.motivation: Physics-based constitutive models oversimplify material properties while data-driven models lack physical consistency, motivating a physics-informed machine learning framework for stress-strain prediction of additively manufactured materials.
summary_en.method: The framework segments stress-strain curves into elastic and plastic regions trained by two LSTMs, embedding Hooke's law for elasticity and Voce/Hollomon hardening laws for plasticity via loss-based or activation-based architectures.
summary_en.result: The activation-based PIML achieves the best performance across four datasets including Ti6Al4V, with MAPE of 10.46% and R² of 0.82.
summary_en.validation: The models are validated on experimental data from additively manufactured Nylon, carbon fiber ABS, AlSi10Mg, and Ti6Al4V.

papers.title: TEST REPORT VERIFICATION METHODS FOR ORTHOPEDIC IMPLANT MATERIALS: a REVIEW
papers.abstract: Accurate verification of material test reports is essential for ensuring the safety, reliability, and regulatory compliance of orthopedic implants. Stainless steel 316L/316LVM and titanium alloys Ti-6Al-4V (Grade 5) and Ti-6Al-4V ELI (Grade 23) are widely used metallic biomaterials governed by international standards such as ISO 5832 and ASTM specifications. This review summarizes the latest verification requirements for chemical composition, mechanical properties, microstructure, and inclusion control as per ISO 5832-1:2024, ASTM F138-19, ISO 5832-3:2021, and ASTM F136-13(2021). Detailed comparison tables and interpretation guidelines are provided to assist manufacturers, regulatory personnel, and quality assurance engineers in evaluating test reports from material suppliers and third-party laboratories.
papers.venue: i-manager s Journal on Material Science

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文仅涉及Ti-6Al-4V植入物材料的测试报告验证标准，而非股骨柄结构设计或力学性能分析。
llm.why_not_core: No stem structural design, lattice architecture, stress-shielding analysis, or fatigue testing; purely a review of material test report verification standards.

summary_zh.motivation: 确保骨科植入物材料测试报告的准确性与合规性
summary_zh.method: 综述ISO 5832和ASTM标准中化学成分、力学性能等验证要求
summary_zh.result: 提供比对表格和解释指南以辅助材料报告审核
summary_zh.validation: 无实验验证，纯文献综述

summary_en.motivation: Accurate verification of material test reports is critical for safety and regulatory compliance of orthopedic implants.
summary_en.method: This review summarizes the latest verification requirements for chemical composition, mechanical properties, and microstructure per ISO and ASTM standards.
summary_en.result: Provides comparison tables and interpretation guidelines for evaluating supplier test reports.
summary_en.validation: No experimental validation; a standard-based literature review.
